cohort: 100 primigravidae with singleton pregnancies at term and inadequate uterine contractions were randomly assigned to either oral misoprostol or intravenous oxytocin.
finding: Both oral misoprostol and intravenous oxytocin effectively augment labor in primigravidae at term, with no significant difference in overall maternal or neonatal outcomes, though misoprostol was associated with higher incidences of fetal distress and tachysystole.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in normal vaginal delivery rates (80% for misoprostol vs. 82% for oxytocin) or cesarean section rates (14% for each) between the two groups.
